criteria.text: Identifies that MSA Section 3.2 makes Bellweather the exclusive provider of all warehousing, freight and delivery services throughout the United States, which goes beyond the signed term sheet's exclusivity limited to last-mile home delivery in the New York City metropolitan area, and recommends narrowing it to the term sheet scope.

Identifies that MSA Section 11.3 carves Customer's Section 10.2 indemnity out of the liability cap while Provider's indemnity stays subject to the 12-month fee cap, explains that this leaves Harrowgate with one-sided unlimited exposure, and recommends removing the carve-out or making it mutual or subject to a cap.

Identifies that DPA Section 9.1 selects Delaware law and Wilmington, Delaware courts, which conflicts with the MSA's New York law and forum. States that the DPA prevails under the MSA order-of-precedence clause, and recommends conforming the DPA to New York law and forum.

Identifies that MSA Section 14.2 auto-renews the agreement for successive 3-year terms unless notice is given within a narrow 15-day window, explains the lock-in risk, and recommends a fix such as shorter renewal terms or a wider or any-time notice right.

Identifies that SOW No. 1 Section 8.2 lets Provider assign without Customer's consent while the MSA assignment clause (Section 17.4) restricts only Customer. Explains the risk of transfer to a competitor or an unvetted party, and recommends a mutual consent requirement or a similar restriction.
States that the MSA order of precedence ranks the Data Processing Addendum above the MSA, with the MSA above the Statement of Work.
States that the MSA general liability cap is the fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim.
Is formatted as a memo addressed to the supervising partner, and for each issue gives the document and section, why it matters, and a recommended fix.
Orders the issues by importance and includes a flag or list of items to raise with the client before the next draft turn.

Does not conclude that the MSA's New York governing-law clause controls data-related disputes over the DPA's Delaware clause, and does not conclude that the two documents are consistent on governing law.
Does not state that the MSA exclusivity clause is consistent with or limited to the term sheet's agreed scope.
